description: Versioned registry of query-conditioned comparability templates (framework document section 3). Each template maps to the protocol facets records must agree on to share a valid comparison set, plus any restrictions. Status semantics are shared and follow consistent query answering over inconsistent databases.

status_semantics.robust: The query answer holds in every valid comparison set (the CQA consistent answer over all repairs).
status_semantics.conditional: The query answer holds in some valid comparison sets but not all; it depends on which protocol you condition on.
status_semantics.insufficient: No valid comparison set is large enough to answer (the missing-facet mass dominates, or the quantity is untestable on this leaderboard).

templates.name: Q_any
templates.question: Which method reports the best value under any protocol?
templates.note: Robust on every leaderboard by construction: with no must-agree facet there is exactly one comparison set, so the naive query can never report uncertainty. This is the failure mode the framing targets, not a finding.

templates.name: Q_official
templates.question: Which method is best under the official (test) protocol?
templates.answer: argmax value restricted to the official protocol
templates.note: Records not on the test split are excluded from every valid comparison set.

templates.name: Q_trend
templates.question: How does the best justified value evolve over publication year?
templates.answer: a per-year sequence of argmax winners
templates.note: Publication year is taken from the arXiv identifier prefix, so it is the preprint year.

templates.name: Q_threshold
templates.question: Does the official champion's lead over the runner-up survive protocol conditioning?

restrictions.detail: champion M* and threshold tau (the best competitor value) are fixed from the principal Q_official comparison set
full-protocol groups {split, metric_surface, unit} in which M* is measured against at least one other method

templates.answer: whether M* strictly exceeds tau in every full-protocol group that measures it against a peer
templates.note: The reference threshold and champion come from the official protocol; robustness is tested by whether that champion still clears the threshold under every other protocol in which it is measured against a peer, which is the faithful CQA reading of a margin query and avoids the vacuous case where the runner-up is trivially below the threshold within its own set. A leaderboard is insufficient when no principal official set exists or M* is measured against a peer under only one protocol.
